questions.prompt: Feature rows exist at timestamps 100, 200 and 300. Which one should a label at event_ts = 250 use?
questions.explanation: Point-in-time correctness: use the newest feature value that existed at the event, i.e. the largest feature_ts ≤ 250, which is 200.

questions.prompt: A model scores 0.99 AUC offline but performs poorly in production. A training feature was joined using each user's latest value. What's the likely cause?
options: Target leakage: features from after the event
questions.explanation: Joining the latest value lets training rows see information from after the event, which isn't available at prediction time. That inflates offline metrics.

questions.prompt: Why group by entity and binary-search instead of scanning all feature rows per label?
options: It cuts the work from O(n·m) to about O((n + m) log m)
It removes the need for a TTL
questions.explanation: Sorting each entity's history once and bisecting for each label replaces a full scan per label with a logarithmic lookup.
